title: DICEBOUND — Quest 6: Ghost of a Chance
status: Implemented in Quest 6 art R1 deployment package
coordinates: Zero-based x,y in data; columns A–M and rows 1–9 in the viewer. A5 is the west doorway and M5 the east doorway.

rules.enemyCounts: Existing six, six, six, six, seven, seven, seven and eight. No roster or stat changes.
rules.normalMovement: Orthogonal movement; solid wall cells blocked.
rules.ghosts: Current engine ignores wall collision while moving, including intermediate turn positions inside walls. No floor-only stopping rule is assumed.
rules.teleporters: Every third enemy phase; at most four Manhattan squares; valid unoccupied landing; no attack in the blink phase.
rules.zombies: After the first defeat, remain inert for one complete enemy phase; then revive once at 50% HP.
rules.water: Shallow water is cosmetic walkable floor; no new hazard or movement cost.
rules.art: Use the same wall cell data for collision and image placement. Whole connected formations, natural alpha edges, coherent material/camera/light, no separate square outlines. Raised art stays within blocked footprints; shadows can soften onto floor.

design.idea: A broken causeway with a short southern turn and a longer northern flank.
design.play: The front zombie draws the party toward the broken pier. Keep a route around the pier so a revival does not pin the rear player against it.
design.threat: Three zombies return once; ordinary dice advance through the same openings as the party.
design.art: Water-darkened causeway stone, raised burial banks and a broken bridge pier. Shallow reflective floor remains walkable.

design.idea: Tomb islands create a return loop around each fight.
design.play: Choose the upper approach or circle the central grave island. Finish a zombie beside an escape route instead of filling the narrow gap with the whole party.
design.threat: Four zombies make the location of a first defeat matter. The two ordinary dice contest the eastern side.
design.art: Distinct connected raised grave islands, water-worn headstones and broken low enclosure walls; no isolated tile-sized rubble spam.

formations.name: West crypt wing / Northwest crypt buttress
East crypt wing / Southeast crypt buttress

design.idea: Opposing crypt wings create a deliberate winding route.
design.play: The party travels below the western wing and above the eastern wing. Ghosts cut directly through those wings, so camping behind a wall is temporary protection from the ordinary foe only.
design.threat: Four ghosts exploit wall crossings, supported by one ordinary die and one zombie.
design.art: Two substantial connected crypt wings with buttresses. Render whole structures, with the walkable central passage visibly open.

design.idea: Two offset screens separate broad landing areas.
design.play: Advance across the lower opening, then turn above the eastern screen. Keep a neighbour within support distance: teleporters can cross a screen into an exposed flank.
design.threat: Three teleporters blink at most four Manhattan squares every third enemy phase and do not attack in that phase. One ghost ignores the screens.
design.art: Broken moorland chapel walls and collapsed burial structures. Use distinct low screens, not tall scenery that hides landing cells.

design.idea: Staggered grave banks turn the approach into an S-shaped route.
design.play: The lower western opening feeds a middle regrouping area before the upper eastern turn. Clear the rear zombie before sending every player around the next corner.
design.threat: Three zombies threaten retreat, while one ghost and one teleporter make a fixed defensive line unreliable.
design.art: Sunken burial terraces with raised stone edges, dense reeds contained on the blocked banks, and a clear shallow-water route.

design.idea: Two offset crossing piers divide the room into three fighting areas.
design.play: Move below the western pier and above the middle pier. A teleporter can skip the middle pier while a ghost approaches through it, so split attention rather than the party.
design.threat: Two ghosts and two teleporters cross the barriers; the zombie and two ordinary dice still take the winding route.
design.art: Connected flooded-bridge abutments and fractured crypt foundations. All gaps between piers remain visually open.

design.idea: Three interlocked screens create the quest’s longest ordinary route.
design.play: Alternate below, above and below the three screens. Use the two-square corridors to pass a teammate, and deal with a returning zombie before committing to the next bend.
design.threat: Two ghosts and two teleporters bypass the long route; two zombies can reopen a fight behind the party. One ordinary die anchors the far passage.
design.art: Long connected ossuary partitions with continuous caps, coherent corners and low silhouettes. No stamped stacks of separate posts.

design.idea: A central sarcophagus splits the approach to an open boss arena.
design.play: Approach the guardian above or below the central obstruction. Keep the eastern arena and a return lane clear while prioritising the ghosts, teleporters and reviving zombies.
design.threat: The existing Boss D20 and seven followers enter together. The boss retains its current one-square collision footprint; no new waves or mechanics are added.
design.art: A drowned mausoleum, low central sarcophagus, joined burial bays and an altar ruin. Leave breathing room around the boss and keep the exit visible.
